newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters dismisses criticism of fiscal plans.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters dismisses criticism of fiscal plans.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters on Thursday said the National-New Zealand First Coalition Government was "diligently assessing its spending proposals" and that work would be well progressed by early February.
He dismissed criticism of the government's fiscal plans.
Earlier, Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said the coalition would not be able to deliver its policy programme within the fiscal parameters it had set out in an agreement.
But Peters said Cullen was "not very good with figures" and had deliberately exaggerated figures in schedule A of the agreement.
"Labour also proposed, according to (party leader) Helen Clark, double the amount of extra expenditure if New Zealand First went with Labour," Peters said in a statement.
"Dr Cullen cannot now recreate himself as a paragon of fiscal rectitude."
